$comment: Shared VfPopover cases, rendered by the Vue adapter at the reference commit, by the current Vue adapter, and by the real Razor adapter with its browser controller. The second catalog whose product DOM is partly outside the case: every panel is found through its trigger's aria-controls - the one declared edge the extractor follows - and compared where it is. A VfDropdown rendered inside a panel or beside a popover is consumer content; the escape stack the two share and the unmount of a nested dropdown are what those cases measure. Initially open cases come first and the page lays cases two per row, so every one fits the first viewport and none is flipped by where it sits. No case opens a dropdown initially: a dropdown's menu is not a followed target, so the isolation of a scenario could not remove it. Open end states are compared three ways and not converged; closed end states converge on the closed case of the same content.

propVocabulary.open: boolean | undefined. Controlled open state. The Vue fixture writes update:open back, as v-model does; the Razor adapter reads it as the initial state and toggles on its own (platformDivergences.razor-has-no-controlled-mode).
propVocabulary.defaultOpen: boolean, default false. The initial uncontrolled state.
propVocabulary.placement: 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end', default 'bottom-start'. floater.js flips within the pair of the same side.
propVocabulary.teleportTo: false renders the panel in place, as disableTeleport does. A selector or an element destination is exercised by the Razor browser gate and the characterization suite.
propVocabulary.disableTeleport: boolean, default false. Renders the panel in place, after the trigger, inside the root.
propVocabulary.closeOnOutsideClick: boolean, default true. Whether a document click outside the trigger and the panel closes it.
propVocabulary.closeOnEscape: boolean, default true. Whether the popover's entry on the shared escape stack closes it; with false the entry still takes the Escape.

contentVocabulary.trigger: The trigger slot: `text` is a plain span; `control` is a real consumer button inside the trigger wrapper. Static on every target: the slot's open/toggle props are Vue-only and pinned by the characterization suite.
contentVocabulary.panel: The default slot: `note` a plain paragraph (.parity-panel-note); `controls` real consumer buttons (.parity-panel-control) - `autofocus` adds the [autofocus] or [data-autofocus] form, `tag: span` makes one an unfocusable span; `dropdown` a real VfDropdown (trigger "Inner", items Edit and Duplicate) teleported to <body>, or in place with `inPlace`. The slot's open/close props are Vue-only.
contentVocabulary.beside: A real VfDropdown rendered before the popover roots, inside the case: `dropdown.inPlace` renders its menu in place, so its open state stays inside the case.
contentVocabulary.after: A consumer control rendered after the roots, inside the case: `control` is a real consumer button, the target of an outside click.

groupVocabulary: A list of sibling popovers rendered side by side in one case, each with its own props; the case-level props are ignored, the content applies to each.

ownershipVocabulary.componentInteractive: The exact number of controls the component itself renders: one trigger wrapper (div, tabindex=0, no role) per instance and one panel (section, role=dialog, tabindex=-1) per open instance - the panel takes focus, which is what makes it a control.
ownershipVocabulary.consumerInteractive: The exact number of consumer focusable elements in the case and in its open panels and menus: a trigger control, an after control, a dropdown trigger, the buttons of an open panel and the items of an open menu.
ownershipVocabulary.consumerInteractiveRoles: The exact number of consumer elements carrying an explicit interactive role: the role=menuitem items of every open dropdown menu.

interactionVocabulary.$comment: A case with an `interaction` is driven with real pointer and key events, alone on the page with its followed panels, then re-measured: snapshot, DOM (with the followed panels) and accessibility tree. The snapshot waits, bounded, for every enter or leave to finish.
interactionVocabulary.steps: clickButton (a real pointer click at the element's centre; `selector` is .vf-popover__trigger, .vf-dropdown__trigger, .parity-trigger-control or .parity-after-control, `index` picks a match; with `through`, the search is inside the panel the case's popover trigger names - .parity-panel-control, .parity-panel-note, .vf-dropdown__trigger), focusButton (likewise), pressKey with ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End, Enter, Space, Tab or Escape, wait (`ms`), scrollWindow (`y`). Every fixture swallows the browser default of a navigation key or Escape the product left unhandled - after recording that it did.
interactionVocabulary.expect: Claims about the snapshot fields of the same name, or `a11y:<role>.<state>` about the tree read after the gesture. `events` lists every open-change of the case's popovers and dropdowns, with the component and its instance. `nestedMenus` records every dropdown in the case or in its open panels; `bodyOverlays` every panel or menu directly in <body>, classified by what still owns it - an overlay no live trigger names is an orphan.
interactionVocabulary.matches: The closed case of the same content whose fresh render the gesture has to land on.

cases.$why: The open half of the relationship contract: aria-controls resolves to a role=dialog tabindex=-1 section outside the case, labelled by the trigger. The panel is the component's second owned control - it takes focus - and the consumer button inside it is the consumer's.

A dropdown opened inside the popover takes the first Escape: it closes, the popover stays open
cases.$why: One escape stack across the two components, LIFO by opening. A popover with a stack of its own would take this Escape and close over the open menu.

cases.title: The second Escape closes the popover and focuses its trigger

A popover opened first and a dropdown opened second: Escape closes the dropdown and leaves the popover open
A closeOnEscape=false popover on top takes the Escape: nothing closes, nothing is prevented, the dropdown below stays open
cases.$why: The reference calls only the top entry of the shared stack. An entry that declines to close still consumes the Escape; a stack that fell through to the next entry would close the dropdown here.

cases.title: The same popover below an open dropdown is simply not reached: the dropdown closes
Enter on the popover trigger closes it over an open nested dropdown: the teleported menu leaves <body> with it
cases.$why: Enter is handled on keydown and prevented, so no click reaches the dropdown's outside listener; only the unmount of the popover's content removes the menu. A Razor controller that is never torn down leaves the menu on the page.

cases.title: After the teardown the next Escape reaches the entry below - the other popover - and not the unmounted dropdown
cases.$why: Two popovers opened by keyboard, the second holding an open dropdown; Enter closes the second. The unmounted dropdown has left the stack, so the Escape closes the first popover. A stale dropdown entry would take this Escape instead and leave the first popover open. Keyboard only: no click reaches the outside listeners of the cases the scenario isolation removed but could not unmount, and those cases' entries sit below both popovers.

cases.title: Enter on an item of the nested menu closes the menu, and the popover with it: the teleported menu is outside the panel
Reopened after the teardown, the popover renders a fresh dropdown that opens and takes the next Escape
